title: Supervised Learning: ID3
instructions: Ten questions. Some have more than one correct answer; select every correct option. Exact match earns one point. Answers are revealed only after submission in the interface.

questions.prompt: In a classification decision tree, what does an internal node ordinarily represent?
options: A test on one input feature
questions.explanation: An internal node asks a question about a feature; branches follow possible answers.

questions.prompt: What is the role of a leaf in a classification decision tree?
options: It always calculates a new entropy
It stores the full training dataset
It chooses the next feature automatically
questions.explanation: A leaf is a terminal decision, typically holding a class label.

questions.prompt: Eight training records have three 'yes' labels and five 'no' labels. Which is their Shannon entropy, approximately?
A candidate split has parent entropy 0.9544 bits and weighted child entropy 0.4056 bits. What is its information gain?
questions.explanation: Information gain is parent entropy minus weighted child entropy: 0.9544 − 0.4056 = 0.5488 bits.

questions.prompt: The candidate root gains are sky: 0.5488, wind: 0.0488 and temperature: 0.0488 bits. Which feature does greedy ID3 choose?
questions.explanation: ID3 chooses the available feature with the largest information gain, here sky.

questions.prompt: In the training subset where sky = rainy, all four outputs are 'no'. What does ID3 do with that branch?
options: Split on the remaining features anyway
Return the most frequent class of the entire dataset
questions.explanation: A pure subset already determines its target label; ID3 stops that branch.

questions.prompt: A learned tree follows these rules: rainy → no; sunny and calm → yes; sunny, windy and warm → yes; sunny, windy and cold → no. What is its prediction for sunny, windy, cold?
questions.explanation: Following sunny → windy → cold reaches the 'no' leaf.

questions.prompt: What happens when every training example reaching a node has the same target label?
options: That node becomes a leaf for the common label
ID3 must ask all remaining questions
questions.explanation: Pure nodes have no remaining classification uncertainty, so the branch terminates.

questions.prompt: Select ALL statements that can be true for a categorical ID3 classification tree.
options: A leaf can represent the predicted class
Two branches can have different depths
A perfect training score guarantees success on unseen inputs
questions.explanation: Leaves hold predictions and branches may terminate at different depths. Categorical features are supported; training fit does not guarantee generalisation.

questions.prompt: A trained tree encounters a feature value absent from the examples at its current node. Select ALL defensible behaviours for an application.
options: Return a documented majority-class fallback and flag uncertainty
Request further information or refer the case to human review
Always assume the unseen value implies 'yes'
Report that the fallback is guaranteed correct
questions.explanation: A documented fallback or a request for review handles unseen values without pretending the prediction is certain.
